variant: source-faithful vision-side SEMA on pretrained BLIP VQA architecture
head_training: BLIP question encoder and answer decoder continue learning even if no expansion
partition_policy: Remove train images byte-identical to official eval; globally group images across tasks before splitting. Eval unchanged.

calibration.selection: First select shared head LR by highest sequential validation AP. At that LR select SEMA threshold maximizing validation AP among settings with AF no worse than sequential; if none, select highest AP but record failed joint criterion. Break ties toward threshold1.0. Never use official eval for selection.

confirmation.training_rows: Same fit split as calibration; never merge held-out validation back into fitting
confirmation.success: Positive mean paired AP gain AND reduced mean paired AF, with actual new-task learning; report each protocol separately. No forced positive conclusion.

limitations: Fixed selected subset and task order; not full benchmark replication or comparison with published CL-MoE/SMoLoRA numbers.
VQA readout is a trainable question/answer encoder-decoder, unlike SEMA's small classification head; answer labels are shared across tasks, so class-incremental masking is inapplicable.

SEMA permits multiple functional phases per task after shallow-to-deep additions. Record exposures; a positive claim about expansion alone requires an additional sequential control matched to those exposures.
BLIP pretrained weights may have seen benchmark images/captions, but no VQA-tuned checkpoint is used.
224-pixel deterministic resize matches SEMA resolution rather than BLIP's 480-pixel VQA finetuning configuration. Generation is greedy32, not answer-vocabulary ranking.
refinement_reason: Initial train-only VQAv2 validation showed large forgetting after20epochs; compare5epochs, a functional epoch count used in official SEMA sema_cifar.json, and an intermediate readout LR. No official eval results used.
